title: Experiment: the walking skeleton's server-side SSE contract
summary: The skeleton was started against a copy of this project's planning content and its `/events` stream read directly over HTTP. The opening frame is exactly "retry: 500\n\n" — a reconnection time and nothing else; no `id:` field is ever sent. A change made while connected was delivered as `data: changed`. A change made during a disconnected window was NOT delivered on reconnect. An idle stream emitted ZERO bytes over six seconds after the opening frame. A write after a client had left did not disturb the server.

facts.workspace: copy of planning-content in a disposable directory, removal verified

omissions.reason: There is no global `EventSource` in this Node build and no browser on this host. Writing a polyfill and measuring it would have measured my own code while implying a browser had been observed. The client half is source-supported only, from the WHATWG specification (EVD-0051..EVD-0054).
The idle stream was observed for six seconds. Whether an intermediary or the OS would drop a longer-idle connection was not exercised, and it is the case a heartbeat would exist to survive.
One reader at a time. Fan-out behaviour across several open pages was not measured.

notes: ⚠️ THE SERVER HALF IS MEASURABLE AND THE CLIENT HALF IS NOT, and the split is stated here so nothing downstream reads a browser claim into this record. What a reconnecting client can RECOVER is a property of what the server sent, and that is what was measured.
